title: COVID-19 coverage from six network and cable news sources in the United States: Representation of misinformation, correction, and portrayals of severity
screen_reason: Manual content analysis of 939 COVID-19-related US broadcast news transcripts (a random 20% weekly sample from ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN, FOX and MSNBC, 1 October 2020 - 30 September 2021), coded for the presence of seven specific widespread false claims identified through the fact-checking sites FactCheck and Snopes (masks not protective; vaccine development rushed; vaccine used to gain money/power; vaccine ineffective; vaccine unnecessary; COVID-19 is a hoax; COVID-19 rates artificially inflated) and for whether each was refuted. The paper reports the share of transcripts containing misinformation overall and per network (Total Misinformation Index 71, 7.56%) plus vaccine-related misinformation (34, 3.6%). Items judged against an external fact-checked ground truth, so CONTENT.

estimates.platform: US broadcast and cable television news transcripts (ABC, CBS, NBC nightly newscasts; four highest-rated 4-10pm shows each on CNN, FOX and MSNBC), retrieved from Nexis Uni
estimates.measure_type: Misinformation statements per 100 COVID-19 news transcripts, all six networks pooled (the paper's Total Misinformation Index)
estimates.denominator: 939 COVID-19-related broadcast news transcripts (a random 20% sample of each week's transcripts from six national networks: ABC 120, CBS 131, NBC 171, CNN 220, FOX 148, MSNBC 149)
estimates.definition: The transcript contained one of seven specific fact-checked false claims: masks are not protective; the vaccine development process was rushed; the vaccine will be used to gain money and power; the COVID-19 vaccine is ineffective; the COVID-19 vaccine is unnecessary; COVID-19 is a hoax; COVID-19 rates are artificially inflated. Presence was coded regardless of whether the claim was subsequently refuted in the same transcript.
estimates.misinfo_def: "specific widespread misinformation (i.e. researchers searched the fact-checking search engines Factcheck.com and Snopes.com to identify specific pieces of misinformation that were widespread enough in the United States to warrant a correction on these sites), and whether or not each piece of misinformation was refuted."
estimates.page_loc: Table 4 (Specific COVID-19 misinformation and correction contained within transcripts), p. 10
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The claim list was derived from the fact-checking search engines FactCheck.com and Snopes.com (claims widespread enough to have been corrected there); presence in each transcript was then coded manually by trained undergraduate coders after 13 hours of structured training on 19 practice articles. Intercoder reliability assessed twice (51 broadcast transcripts, then 12 March-2021 transcripts) with all variables meeting Gwet's AC >= .70: masks not protective 1.00/.99, COVID-19 is a hoax .81/.94, rates artificially inflated .95/.98, vaccine-related misinformation .93/.91 (Table 1). Gwet's AC was chosen because several codes were low-prevalence.
estimates.moderator_quote: Nexis Uni was used to search all transcripts from nightly network newscasts on ABC, CBS, and NBC and selected nighttime cable news network shows on CNN, FOX, and MSNBC using search terms "COVID" and "coronavirus" to generate lists of all transcripts that included at least two sentences that said something about COVID-19 between October 1, 2020, and September 30, 2021. ... A random integer set generator (random.org) was used to select a 20% sample of each week's transcripts to be coded. The final total sample used or the present study included 939 coded transcripts from ABC (n = 120), CBS (n = 131), NBC (n = 171), CNN (n = 220), FOX (n = 148), and MSNBC (n = 149).
estimates.notes: IMPORTANT: the Total Misinformation Index is the SUM of the seven misinformation-type counts divided by the number of transcripts ("The sum of all misinformation included in all transcripts was calculated as a total misinformation index for each station"), so a transcript carrying two different false claims counts twice. It is therefore a rate per transcript and a slight upper bound on the share of transcripts containing at least one false claim. The value is stated verbatim by the authors, so it is kept under R8. This row and the six per-network rows below are NESTED (the network rows decompose this total): an analyst must use one level, not both. A further caveat the paper stresses: 46 of the 71 statements (64.8%) were refuted within the same transcript, and on CNN and MSNBC most misinformation appears to have been raised in order to correct it, whereas none of FOX's 16 statements were corrected. source_quote is the Table 4 Total Misinformation Index row together with the Total Refutation Index row immediately below it, quoted as one contiguous span in column order ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN, FOX, MSNBC, Total; this row reads all six networks pooled (Total column).

estimates.platform: US broadcast and cable television news transcripts, six networks pooled
estimates.measure_type: % of COVID-19 news transcripts containing misinformation about the COVID-19 vaccine
estimates.value_raw: Misinformation about the COVID-19 vaccine: 34 (3.6%) of 939 transcripts (ABC 2 (1.7%), CBS 2 (1.5%), NBC 5 (2.9%), CNN 13 (5.9%), FOX 3 (2.0%), MSNBC 9 (6.0%))
estimates.denominator: 939 COVID-19-related broadcast news transcripts from six national networks
estimates.definition: The transcript contained vaccine-related misinformation (the major code 'Vaccine-related misinformation, including all subcode combinations'; subcodes include the vaccine development process was rushed, the vaccine will be used to gain money and power, the vaccine is ineffective, the vaccine is unnecessary).
estimates.misinfo_def: "researchers searched the fact-checking search engines Factcheck.com and Snopes.com to identify specific pieces of misinformation that were widespread enough in the United States to warrant a correction on these sites"
estimates.page_loc: Table 2 (COVID-19 severity, misinformation, and correction coverage), p. 8
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same fact-check-derived claim list and manual coding; the vaccine-misinformation index had the highest reliability of the coded variables (Gwet's AC .93 at time 1, .91 at time 2).
estimates.moderator_quote: The codebook was expanded in the fall of 2021 to capture additional COVID-19 discourse that did not yet exist when the initial codebook was created (e.g. vaccine-specific information).
estimates.notes: definition_variant = true: a topic-restricted version (vaccine misinformation only) of the overall misinformation measure in the same country x source cell, coded topic = vaccines. Table 2 counts TRANSCRIPTS (34/939 = 3.6%), whereas Table 4's index counts statements; the four vaccine subcodes listed in Table 4 sum to only 16, so Table 2's major code evidently covers additional subcodes not itemised in Table 4. Nested with the pooled row, so do not pool the two. source_quote is the Table 2 'Misinformation about the COVID-19 vaccine' row, whose label the PDF wraps onto the following line; column order is ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN, FOX, MSNBC, Total.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) 'Misinformation discussed as a problem' (Table 2: 138, 14.7% overall; ABC 5 (4.2%), CBS 6 (4.6%), NBC 8 (4.7%), CNN 42 (19.1%), FOX 29 (19.6%), MSNBC 48 (32.2%)) and 'President Trump as a source of misinformation' (63, 6.7%; FOX 0) measure coverage ABOUT the misinformation problem, not the presence of misinformation, so no rows. (2) Correction figures are recorded but not extracted as prevalence: Total Refutation Index 46 (64.8%) of the 71 statements overall (ABC 0, CBS 2 (66.7%), NBC 3 (100%), CNN 24 (96.0%), FOX 0, MSNBC 17 (77.3%)) and 'Total corrected misinformation' 46 (4.90%) of transcripts. The complementary UNCORRECTED share (71 - 46 = 25, 2.66%) is a complement I would have to compute, which R8 forbids, even though it is arguably the quantity of interest for audience exposure. (3) Per-claim rows in Table 4 are recorded here rather than as separate rows (each has a tiny numerator): masks not protective 17 (1.8%), vaccine development rushed 4 (.4%), vaccine used to gain money/power 2 (.2%), vaccine ineffective 8 (.9%), vaccine unnecessary 2 (.2%), COVID-19 is a hoax 25 (2.7%), rates artificially inflated 13 (1.4%). (4) All disease-severity results (Tables 2 and 3) are coverage-content measures unrelated to veracity. (5) Figures cited from elsewhere and excluded by R8: KFF trust percentages (Democrats 72%/65%/56%; Republicans FOX 49%) and the KFF headline that 78% of the public believes or is unsure about at least one false statement. (6) The six per-network rows above and the pooled row are nested; an analyst must pick one level.

rob.design: Manual content analysis of a probability sample within a defined frame. Frame: all Nexis Uni transcripts from ABC, CBS and NBC nightly newscasts and four highest-rated 4-10pm shows each on CNN, FOX and MSNBC containing 'COVID'/'coronavirus' and at least two sentences about COVID-19, 1 October 2020 - 30 September 2021. A weekly sampling frame was built and a random 20% of each week's transcripts selected with random.org, giving 939 coded transcripts (ABC 120, CBS 131, NBC 171, CNN 220, FOX 148, MSNBC 149). Five trained undergraduate coders (two assigned exclusively to broadcast content, one shared), 13 hours of structured training on 19 practice articles, disagreements resolved with the codebook authors. Two intercoder reliability assessments (n = 51 broadcast transcripts; n = 12 March-2021 transcripts), all variables meeting Gwet's AC >= .70 (Table 1 values .71-1.00). Misinformation items were fact-check-derived specific claims coded present/absent, with refutation coded separately. Limitations acknowledged: only 20% of content coded, low prevalence of some codes makes results sensitive to a handful of atypical transcripts, and shows were collapsed to network level. Funded by NIA 3R01AG063954-02S1.
